newsitem.title: UK: Palm oil lower in Europe despite bullish data.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil lower in Europe despite bullish data.

text.p: Palm oil prices were lower on the Eurpoean vegetable oil market on Wednesday despite seemingly bullish data from PORLA.
The Malaysian Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) put end-December stocks at 792,687 tonnes against 955,958 at end-November.
Production was put at 637,865 tonnes, down from November's 762,539, while exports were seen at 637,899 against 636,554.
Traders said the data seemed to be bullish with lower than expected stocks, but added that this seemed to them to be due more to a very high local disappearance rate than exports.
"There is a big question mark hanging over the local disappearence rate..." said a trader.
Traders said the local palm oil disappearance was in the region of 163,000 tonnes during December, against 124,000 tonnes in November and 98,000 tonnes during October.
"The 163,000 tonnes seems very high against the previous months' figures which makes us think there will be a revision next month," said another trader.
News that China has cut its import duty on finished palm oil to 12 percent from 18 percent, back-dated to January 1, 1997, boosted early prices.
But the rally soon fizzled out, and at midday crude palm oil was offered $7.50 to $2.50 down.
In Early trading Feb fetched $567.50 and Apr/Jun $562.50 a tonne cif.
Among products RBD palm oil was $2.50 down after Feb traded at $562.50 while olein was unchanged after Feb fetched $592.50 and $597.50 and Mar $590 a tonne fob Malaysian ports.
Lauric oils were mixed with coconut oil $5 down to $5 up and palmkernel oil $7.50 higher.
Soft oils were steady despite the easier Chicago close mainly due to a strong dollar.
At midday Dutch soyoil was 0.50 guilders up while rapeoil was unchanged to 0.25 guilders higher.
Rape oil's premium over soy oil, based on sellers' prices, was one to 0.50 guilders at midday against 1.50 to 0.75 at Tuesday's close.
